t: This is Camden Square, a rectangular square north of central Camden, running parallel to Camden Road. St Paul's Church stands at the north end, and the London Irish Centre, which has served the borough's Irish community for over sixty years, is at the south end. The square has a playground and a dog-walking area. Its residents have included the artist Lawrence Alma-Tadema and the singer Amy Winehouse. The wood-engraver Orlando Jewitt and the dramatist Robert Reece, who adapted the operetta Les cloches de Corneville, both died here, and the illustrator Maud Horman-Fisher lived here.
